title: Hammond's challenge in Kansas City
summary: Jones explains that Kansas City musicians were content at $17.50 and not interested in New York money, but Hammond had a flexibility that penetrated.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: "Where's Basie?" I said, "I'll find him." This man, after we had got through doing things to do what we were doing and - I was with a lot of maneuvering with John Hammond. You must remember that John Hammond with the peoples that he had to get in the 48 states, villages and hamlets - he had just come out of a trauma. He had gone through the Bessie Smiths, he had gone through the Billie Holidays in the early days in Harlem, but to come out in that particular geographical section of the country with the peoples the way they think - I mean it wasn't a suspicious nature, it wasn't that they wasn't used to seeing white people; but with what he had in his mind to do, they didn't have no minding that because Basie's band belonged to Kansas City and they could care less if he was going to pay somebody $1,000 a week. We were doing all right; we were making $17.50 so we don't need nobody. We don't care nothing about $100 a week. But he had a flexibility that penetrated and we are dealing with a challenger of intelligence now. People, as I said, had just come out of Depression. We come into the world with nothing; we go out with nothing. We do more good than we do evil. But when we designate certain peoples to do certain things and behind our backs they don't do it, we get blamed for it. It's the same way with the President of the United States. He can't tell all the Governors and the Senators what to do. He can just put
it out there but if they don't do it for the 50 states, that's not his fault.
